Why Towels Smell After Washing (and How to Fix It)

Guides from Better Everyday

A towel can come out of the laundry looking perfectly clean and still develop a musty smell when it gets wet again. The cause is usually not a lack of fragrance. Moisture left in the fabric, detergent residue, or an unclean washer can all contribute. The practical fix is to clean the fabric thoroughly, rinse well, and dry it completely.

Why do clean towels smell musty?

Towels absorb plenty of water, and thick loops of fabric can stay damp for hours. A towel tossed in a hamper, left in the washer, or folded before it is fully dry provides conditions in which unwanted odors can develop.

Another common issue is buildup. More detergent does not always mean cleaner laundry; too much can be difficult to rinse away. Some fabric softeners can also leave a coating that affects absorbency.

  • Damp towels left in a pile or closed laundry basket.
  • A washer overloaded with thick items.
  • Too much detergent or fabric softener.
  • A damp washing-machine gasket or detergent drawer.
  • Towels stored before they are completely dry.

How to remove a musty smell from towels

Before changing wash settings, check the towel's care label and your machine's manual.

  1. Separate the musty towels from delicate clothing and do not pack the drum tightly.
  2. Check the care label; select an appropriate normal wash cycle and water temperature.
  3. Add a measured amount of laundry detergent according to the label and machine instructions.
  4. Skip fabric softener for this wash if you suspect buildup.
  5. Use an additional rinse only if residue remains and your machine offers the option.
  6. Remove the towels as soon as the cycle ends and dry them completely before putting them away.

If an odor persists, repeat with a suitable laundry detergent or laundry-care product used exactly as its label directs. Do not add random mixtures of household chemicals to a wash. In particular, never mix chlorine bleach with vinegar, ammonia or other cleaners.

Dry towels thoroughly after every use

Hang used towels over a wide bar or rack where air can circulate instead of bunching them on a hook. In a humid bathroom, a fan, open door or a better-ventilated drying area may help.

After laundry, use the dryer setting allowed by the care label, or space towels apart on a drying rack. They should feel dry all the way through before folding.

Could the washing machine be causing the odor?

If several kinds of laundry smell unpleasant right after washing, inspect the machine. Check visible detergent buildup, the drum, the door seal on front-loading washers, and any filter the manufacturer says is user-serviceable.

Run the manufacturer's recommended cleaning cycle when needed. Let the drum and detergent drawer dry between loads if your appliance instructions allow it. Never dismantle components or mix cleaning chemicals unless the manufacturer specifically says it is safe.

Should you use fabric softener on towels?

Fabric softener is not required to get towels clean. Overuse can leave residue and may reduce absorbency. If your towels feel waxy or stop absorbing water well, wash them without softener for a while and use the right amount of detergent.

Do not use extra detergent to cover up smells. Correct washing, rinsing, and drying are generally more useful than stronger perfume.

Everyday habits that keep towels fresher

  • Give each towel enough hanging space between uses.
  • Wash towels regularly, and sooner when heavily soiled.
  • Keep wet towels out of closed hampers until they dry.
  • Avoid overcrowding the washing machine.
  • Move laundry promptly from washer to dryer or rack.
  • Store towels only after they are completely dry.

When should you replace a towel?

A lingering smell does not automatically mean a towel needs replacing. First try an appropriate wash and thorough drying. If it remains badly worn, has damaged fibers, or repeatedly develops an odor despite proper care, replacing it may be more practical.

For sensitive skin or recurring irritation, choose a suitable laundry product and consider professional medical advice if symptoms persist.

Frequently asked questions

Why do towels smell fine dry but bad when wet?

Moisture can make trapped odors more noticeable. Residue and poor drying may contribute; a proper wash, thorough rinse and complete drying often help.

Is more detergent the answer to smelly towels?

Usually not. Too much detergent can be hard to rinse out. Follow the dosage instructions for your machine, load and water conditions.

Can I mix vinegar and bleach to clean towels?

No. Never mix chlorine bleach with vinegar, ammonia or other household cleaning chemicals. Follow the product label.
